raw_case_text: A 22-month-old girl presented to us with 8-day fever (40 C), and mild cough. On examination, she had hepatosplenomegaly. Past medical history included failure to thrive, but normal neurological development. She was the first child of a non-consanguineous marriage. She had normal brown hair and normal skin. There was no family history of albinism. On physical examination, she was stunted, pale, and had non-tender hepatomegaly of 5-6 cm; the spleen was palpable 4 cm below the left costal margin as confirmed by abdominal ultrasound. The WBC count was 5100/mm3 (ANC 1200/mm3), Hb 9.1 g/dl, and platelets 47.000/mm3. She had mild hypertransaminasemia and hypoalbuminemia. Ferritin was 1134 ng/ml. Soluble IL-2 receptor (sCD25) was 3183 UI/ml. Blood cultures were negative. Serum immunoglobulins and lymphocyte subsets were normal. Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) serology yielded seroreactivity (positive IgM and IgG anti-VCA) with negative IgG anti-EBNA. EBV viral load was 637 copies/ml. Leishmania serology showed both negative immunochromatography and indirect immunofluorescence. Conversely, serum ELISA was slightly positive. Leishmanial antigen in the urine was negative. Bone marrow aspiration revealed hemophagocytosis. The patient worsened clinically, with persistent malaise, progressive splenomegaly, and petechial rash on her chest and legs. Subsequent investigations were WBC 4800/mm3 (ANC 800/mm3), Hb 6.8 g/dl and platelets 27000/mm3, triglycerides 686 mg/dl, ferritin 3849 ng/ml, and sCD25 3596 UI/ml with normal clotting tests as well as perforin expression by flow-cytometry. Hair microscopy was not performed because clinical features of albinism were not present neither in our patient nor in her family. HLH-2004 protocol was started. The following day, Leishmania Polymerase Chain Reaction was done where Leishmanial DNA was detected by nested PCR.) This was confirmed on a bone marrow aspirate as well. Standard therapy with liposomal amphotericin B (3 mg/kg/day IV on days 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 14, and 21) was given. The patient completed HLH-2004 protocol, except for 2 doses of etoposide due to clinical and laboratory improvement without evidence of underlying primary HLH. At 30 month follow up, there is no evidence of relapse. As CD107a degranulation assay was not performed (just normal intracytoplasmic pattern of perforin staining), primary HLH is not absolutely discarded as a differential diagnosis.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 22-month-old girl presented with an 8-day history of high fever up to 40 C and mild cough.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The child presented with 8 days of 40 C fever and mild cough and was found to have hepatosplenomegaly, cytopenias, and bone marrow hemophagocytosis. Her condition worsened in the hospital with persistent malaise, progressive splenomegaly, a petechial rash on the chest and legs, and deepening pancytopenia and hyperferritinemia.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of failure to thrive with normal neurodevelopment; first child of non-consanguineous parents; no personal or family history of albinism.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for high fever, mild cough, malaise, and subsequent petechial rash on the chest and legs.

objective.physical_examination: Stunted growth, pallor, normal brown hair and skin pigmentation, non-tender hepatomegaly (5-6 cm below costal margin), and splenomegaly (4 cm below left costal margin, progressing during admission), later accompanied by a petechial rash over the chest and lower extremities.
objective.routine_investigations: Initial labs showed WBC 5,100/mm3 (ANC 1,200/mm3), Hb 9.1 g/dL, platelets 47,000/mm3, mild hypertransaminasemia, hypoalbuminemia, and ferritin 1,134 ng/mL, worsening to WBC 4,800/mm3 (ANC 800/mm3), Hb 6.8 g/dL, platelets 27,000/mm3, triglycerides 686 mg/dL, and ferritin 3,849 ng/mL with normal coagulation tests. Blood cultures, urinary Leishmania antigen, and Leishmania immunochromatography and IIF serologies were negative, Leishmania serum ELISA was borderline/slightly positive, and EBV serology was positive for anti-VCA IgM and IgG (anti-EBNA IgG negative) with EBV viral load 637 copies/mL. Abdominal ultrasound confirmed hepatosplenomegaly.
objective.advanced_workup: Soluble IL-2 receptor (sCD25) rose from 3,183 UI/mL to 3,596 UI/mL; serum immunoglobulins, lymphocyte subsets, and flow-cytometric intracellular perforin expression were normal. Bone marrow aspiration demonstrated hemophagocytosis, and nested PCR on peripheral blood and bone marrow aspirate detected Leishmania DNA.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Nested PCR on peripheral blood and bone marrow aspirate confirmed Visceral Leishmaniasis-associated secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) co-existing with mild acute EBV viremia (637 copies/mL). Combined treatment with intravenous liposomal amphotericin B (3 mg/kg/day on days 1-5, 14, and 21) and the HLH-2004 protocol (with the final 2 doses of etoposide omitted due to rapid clinical and hematologic recovery) resulted in complete remission with no relapse at 30-month follow-up.
